# B2C Support

`customer_support.model.b2c` · model · parent `—`

> Supporting individual consumers. Requester, buyer and payer collapse into one person, which removes the whole B2B problem of a hidden economic audience and replaces it with a harder one: volume. The queue is large, the median contact is simple and repetitive, and the economics only work if most contacts never reach a human. Sentiment is public — a consumer who is unhappy has a review site and a social account, and the escalation path runs through an audience rather than through a committee. Contacts arrive in every channel at once and the same person will open three of them about one problem while waiting. The error carried in from B2B is per-ticket craftsmanship. A bespoke, carefully worded investigation for one consumer is not thoroughness at this volume; it is capacity taken from the queue behind it. The corresponding B2C-native error is assuming volume means the contacts are trivial — a frozen account or a missing delivery is not a small problem to the person it happened to, and tone failures here are the ones that end up screenshotted.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | the consumer themselves — buyer, user and payer in one person, with no procurement process and no patience for one |
| typical_resolution_hours | 4 |
| volume_shape | very high volume, low median complexity, strongly diurnal, with campaign-, outage- and season-driven spikes an order of magnitude above baseline |
| staffing_model | pooled agents on shared queues, no formal tiers, specialist pods for fraud/billing |
| coverage | extended hours seven days, often 24x7 on chat |
| automation_level | high — bots, help centre and in-product answers are expected to resolve the majority before a human is involved |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.ticket`

Requires `channel`, `queue`


> Channel is load-bearing in B2C in a way it is not in B2B: the same person contacting by chat, app store review and DM is one problem and three tickets, and the merge decision cannot be made without knowing where each arrived from.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.customer_sentiment`


> Sentiment here has an audience. A consumer's anger is a public risk as well as a service failure, which is why sentiment_analysis is emphasised and why the same polarity reading justifies a different response than it would in B2B.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.requester`


> The requester IS the account. Anything the canonical object models as inherited from an organisation — entitlement, locale, history — is a property of this one person.
